title_en: Zhang Aimin, Li Nan, et al. — illegal hunting, capturing, purchasing, transporting, and selling of precious and endangered wildlife
ruling_gist_en: The indiscriminate hunting and illegal trading of wild animals undermine the integrity of the food chain and biodiversity, thereby damaging the entire ecological environment. It is necessary to strengthen criminal judicial protection for wild animals. A person who commits any of the acts of illegally hunting, illegally purchasing, transporting, or selling state-key protected wild animals shall constitute a crime.

full_text_en:
Zhang Aimin, Li Nan, et al. — illegal hunting, purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife case

Ruling Summary

Random hunting and illegal trading of wildlife damage the integrity of the biological chain and biodiversity, thereby undermining the entire ecological environment. It is necessary to strengthen criminal judicial protection of wildlife. An actor who commits any act of illegal hunting, illegal purchasing, transporting, or selling of national key protected wildlife shall constitute a crime.

Procuratorial Authority: People's Procuratorate of Yunlong District, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendants: Zhang Aimin, Li Nan, Wang Jie, Han Dongdong, Huang Dalin, Wang Zhi, Gao Jiangtao, Liu Xiyuan, Wang Gao, Lai Zhengwen, Deng Yu, Tian Jing, Wang Xueyi, Xu Tengyan, Chu Shuo.

The People's Procuratorate of Yunlong District, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province initiated a public prosecution with the People's Court of Gulou District, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province, charging the defendants Zhang Aimin, Li Nan, Wang Jie, Han Dongdong, Huang Dalin, Wang Zhi, Gao Jiangtao, Liu Xiyuan, Wang Gao, Lai Zhengwen, Deng Yu, Tian Jing, Wang Xueyi, Xu Tengyan, and Chu Shuo with the crime of illegal hunting, illegal purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife.

The People's Court of Gulou District, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province found the following facts at first instance:

From May 2015 to January 2016, the defendants Zhang Aimin, Li Nan, Huang Dalin, Wang Zhi, Gao Jiangtao, Liu Xiyuan, Wang Jie, Han Dongdong, Wang Gao, Lai Zhengwen, Deng Yu, Tian Jing, Wang Xueyi, Xu Tengyan, and Chu Shuo became acquainted with each other through Tencent QQ, WeChat and other online communication platforms, including the "Suzhou Falcon Exchange Group" established by Zhang Aimin, the "Northwest Falcon Hunting Group" established by Wang Xueyi, the "Xi'an Falcon Hunting Group," and the "Pet Marmoset Trading Exchange Group." They used payment methods such as Alipay, WeChat, and bank transfers, and used long-distance passenger vehicles to transport illegally hunted wildlife for sale or illegal purchase. Upon appraisal, the wildlife involved included: five golden eagles (*Aquila chrysaetos*), a national first-class key protected wildlife species; one upland buzzard (*Buteo hemilasius*), four falcon species including saker falcon (*Falco cherrug*) and peregrine falcon (*Falco peregrinus*), four Eurasian sparrowhawks (*Accipiter nisus*), one besra sparrowhawk (*Accipiter virgatus*), one rhesus macaque (*Macaca mulatta*), and one steppe eagle (*Aquila nipalensis*), all national second-class key protected wildlife species; and one reticulated python (*Python reticulatus*), a wildlife species listed in Appendix II of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). Specifically, defendant Zhang Aimin illegally purchased five golden eagles and one reticulated python, and illegally transported and sold two of the golden eagles and one upland buzzard; defendant Li Nan illegally purchased, transported, and sold five golden eagles; defendant Wang Jie illegally purchased, transported, and sold three golden eagles, and illegally purchased and sold one saker falcon and one rhesus macaque; defendant Han Dongdong illegally purchased one golden eagle and illegally transported one golden eagle; defendant Huang Dalin illegally purchased one reticulated python, two Eurasian sparrowhawks, one besra sparrowhawk, and one peregrine falcon, and illegally sold the reticulated python; defendant Gao Jiangtao illegally hunted one saker falcon and illegally purchased one saker falcon; defendant Liu Xiyuan illegally hunted two Eurasian sparrowhawks and sold and transported them; defendant Lai Zhengwen illegally purchased two Eurasian sparrowhawks; defendant Wang Zhi illegally transported and sold one golden eagle; defendant Wang Gao illegally purchased one golden eagle; defendant Tian Jing illegally purchased, transported, and sold one saker falcon; defendant Wang Xueyi illegally transported and sold one saker falcon; defendant Deng Yu illegally purchased one upland buzzard; defendant Xu Tengyan illegally purchased one steppe eagle; defendant Chu Shuo illegally purchased one common kestrel (*Falco tinnunculus*).

The People's Court of Gulou District, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province held at first instance:

Wildlife resources belong to the state and are the common wealth of all humankind, possessing significant ecological, economic, and scientific value. Protecting and rationally utilizing wildlife resources are of great significance for maintaining ecological balance, improving the natural environment, and promoting comprehensive, coordinated, and sustainable economic and social development. However, due to overhunting, habitat loss, black market trading, and other factors, the extinction rate of wildlife is gradually increasing. The precious and endangered wildlife that are the objects of the crime in this case, such as golden eagles and saker falcons, are species at the top of the biological chain. They have low reproductive rates, are scarce in number, and are highly susceptible to environmental impacts. If random hunting and illegal trading continue, they will become even more endangered, damaging the integrity of the biological chain and biodiversity, and thereby undermining the entire ecological environment. Therefore, enhanced criminal judicial protection is even more necessary. After an actor illegally purchases national key protected wildlife, even if they do not sell for profit but instead keep the wildlife for themselves, or if they do not profit from the illegal transportation or sale of national key protected wildlife, their actions still infringe upon precious and endangered wildlife resources and should be punished as a crime.

The defendants Zhang Aimin, Li Nan, Wang Jie, Han Dongdong, Huang Dalin, Wang Zhi, Gao Jiangtao, Liu Xiyuan, Wang Gao, Lai Zhengwen, Deng Yu, Tian Jing, Wang Xueyi, Xu Tengyan, and Chu Shuo violated the state's regulations on the protection of precious and endangered wildlife. Knowing that the wildlife were national key protected species, they hunted, purchased, transported, or sold them respectively. Among them, the acts of defendants Zhang Aimin and Li Nan reached the level of "especially serious circumstances," and the acts of Wang Jie and Han Dongdong reached the level of "serious circumstances." The acts of defendants Zhang Aimin, Li Nan, Wang Jie, and Tian Jing respectively constituted the crime of illegally purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife; the act of defendant Huang Dalin constituted the crime of illegally purchasing and selling precious and endangered wildlife; the acts of defendants Wang Zhi and Wang Xueyi respectively constituted the crime of illegally transporting and selling precious and endangered wildlife; the acts of defendants Wang Gao, Lai Zhengwen, Deng Yu, Xu Tengyan, and Chu Shuo respectively constituted the crime of illegally purchasing precious and endangered wildlife.

The crime of illegally purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife is a selective charge. "Purchasing" includes buying for purposes such as profit or personal use; "transporting" includes methods of conveyance such as carrying, mailing, using others, or employing vehicles; "selling" includes selling and processing or utilizing for profit purposes. Where a defendant commits any one or several of the above acts, they shall be convicted based on the act(s) actually committed. Article 23 of the Wildlife Protection Law of the People's Republic of China provides that the transportation or carrying of national key protected wildlife or their products out of a county must be approved by the wildlife administrative department of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, or by a unit authorized by it. When defendant Han Dongdong committed the illegal purchase act, he also used long-distance passenger vehicles to transport the precious and endangered wildlife to another location at the request of Zhang Aimin without administrative approval, thus committing an illegal transport act. Therefore, the act of defendant Han Dongdong constitutes the crime of illegally purchasing and transporting precious and endangered wildlife.

Paragraph 1 of Article 341 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China includes two separate crimes: the crime of illegally hunting and killing precious and endangered wildlife, and the crime of illegally purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife and products thereof. Defendant Gao Jiangtao committed the illegal hunting of one national second-class key protected saker falcon and the illegal purchase of another saker falcon, constituting two different criminal acts and violating two crimes simultaneously. Accordingly, he should be punished for both the crime of illegally hunting precious and endangered wildlife and the crime of illegally purchasing precious and endangered wildlife, with concurrent punishment for multiple crimes.

Defendant Liu Xiyuan illegally hunted two national second-class key protected Eurasian sparrowhawks and illegally transported and sold them to defendant Lai Zhengwen. The objects of the three criminal acts (hunting, transporting, selling) were the same, and the purpose of the hunting was also to sell. Therefore, the criminal acts of defendant Liu Xiyuan were committed for a single criminal purpose through multiple criminal acts, and there was a means-end relationship between the acts. This constitutes an implicated offense under criminal law, and punishment should be imposed only for the more serious crime. In this case, it is appropriate to convict and sentence him for the crime of illegally hunting precious and endangered wildlife.

Defendants Zhang Aimin, Wang Jie, Wang Zhi, Han Dongdong, Tian Jing, and Wang Xueyi played equivalent roles in the related joint crimes and were all principals. Defendant Li Nan had previously been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment for an intentional crime. Less than five years after completing that sentence, he committed another crime punishable by fixed-term imprisonment, and it was the same type of crime, constituting recidivism. He was accordingly given a heavier punishment as provided by law. In the criminal act where defendant Zhang Aimin purchased a golden eagle from Li Nan for RMB 3,500, the act was an attempted crime; accordingly, a lighter punishment was imposed for that criminal fact. At the time of illegally selling a saker falcon in May 2015, defendant Wang Jie had already reached the age of seventeen but was not yet eighteen, thus was a minor; accordingly, a lighter punishment was imposed for that criminal fact. Defendant Wang Gao voluntarily surrendered to the public security authorities and truthfully confessed all criminal facts, constituting voluntary surrender; accordingly, a lighter punishment was imposed. After being brought to justice, defendants Li Nan, Huang Dalin, Wang Zhi, Gao Jiangtao, Liu Xiyuan, Han Dongdong, Lai Zhengwen, Deng Yu, Tian Jing, Wang Xueyi, Xu Tengyan, and Chu Shuo truthfully confessed their criminal facts, constituting truthful confessions; accordingly, lighter punishments were imposed. Defendants Zhang Aimin and Wang Jie voluntarily admitted guilt in court; accordingly, relatively lighter punishments were imposed. Defendants Wang Gao and Han Dongdong illegally purchased golden eagles and kept them for personal raising, which constituted a completed crime. After the case of co-participant Zhang Aimin was discovered, they surrendered the golden eagles they had raised to the Laiwu Soaring Raptor Rescue Center and the Forest Public Security Bureau of Minquan County, Henan Province. In light of these circumstances, relatively lighter punishments were imposed on the two defendants.

Considering that defendants Wang Gao, Lai Zhengwen, Deng Yu, Tian Jing, Wang Xueyi, Xu Tengyan, and Chu Shuo had relatively minor criminal circumstances, good attitudes toward admitting guilt, and that imposing a suspended sentence would not have a major adverse impact on the communities where they reside and would not cause them to endanger society again, a suspended sentence may be imposed on the above defendants.

In summary, based on each defendant's criminal facts, nature of the crime, circumstances, and degree of harm to society, the People's Court of Gulou District, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Paragraph 1 of Article 341, Paragraphs 1 and 3 of Article 17, Article 23, Paragraph 1 of Article 25, Paragraphs 1 and 4 of Article 26, Paragraph 1 of Article 65, Paragraphs 1 and 3 of Article 67, Paragraphs 1 and 3 of Article 69, Paragraphs 1 and 3 of Article 72, Paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 73, and Article 64 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, as well as Articles 1, 2, Paragraph 1(1) of Article 3, and Paragraph 2(1) of Article 3 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Destroying Wildlife Resources, rendered the following judgment on October 10, 2016:

1. Defendant Zhang Aimin is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of eleven years and six months, and fined RMB 40,000.

2. Defendant Li Nan is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of eleven years, and fined RMB 35,000.

3. Defendant Wang Jie is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of seven years, and fined RMB 20,000.

4. Defendant Han Dongdong is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing and transporting precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of five years, and fined RMB 15,000.

5. Defendant Huang Dalin is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing and selling precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of four years, and fined RMB 10,000.

6. Defendant Wang Zhi is convicted of the crime of illegally transporting and selling precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of two years, and fined RMB 7,000.

7. Defendant Gao Jiangtao is convicted of the crime of illegally hunting precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, and fined RMB 3,000; and convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, and fined RMB 3,000. The combined sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of one year and six months, and a fine of RMB 6,000.

8. Defendant Liu Xiyuan is convicted of the crime of illegally hunting precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year and six months, and fined RMB 6,000.

9. Defendant Wang Gao is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, suspended for two years, and fined RMB 5,000.

10. Defendant Lai Zhengwen is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, suspended for two years, and fined RMB 5,000.

11. Defendant Deng Yu is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, suspended for one year and six months, and fined RMB 3,000.

12. Defendant Tian Jing is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing, transporting, and selling precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, suspended for one year and six months, and fined RMB 3,000.

13. Defendant Wang Xueyi is convicted of the crime of illegally transporting and selling precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, suspended for one year and six months, and fined RMB 3,000.

14. Defendant Xu Tengyan is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, suspended for one year, and fined RMB 3,000.

15. Defendant Chu Shuo is convicted of the crime of illegally purchasing precious and endangered wildlife and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year, suspended for one year, and fined RMB 3,000.

16. The illegal gains of the defendants shall be recovered by the public security organs in accordance with law and turned over to the state treasury; the seized wildlife involved in the case shall be transferred by the public security organs to the relevant authorities for disposal in accordance with law.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, none of the fifteen defendants filed an appeal within the statutory appeal period, and the prosecutorial authority did not file a protest. The judgment of first instance has become legally effective.
